title: Shalom V'Achdus
hebrewTitle: שָׁלוֹם וְאַחְדוּת, אַהֲבַת חֲבֵרִים, וְלָדוּן הַכֹּל לְכַף זְכוּת

segments.en: Otzar HaYirah — Treasury of Awe | Volume IV (נ–ת)

The longest chapter since Tzadik, at 68 entries. The chapter's thesis is that peace is not merely a social virtue — it is the cosmic mechanism through which separated fragments of the divine light can be received without shattering. Every soul of Israel is a vessel — and the light of G-dliness requires all vessels assembled together in love and peace to be received safely. This is why the Torah required 600,000 present at Sinai, and why love of one's neighbor is declared the great principle of the Torah.

A recurring and powerful idea is the interplay between truth and peace (entry 20): Hashem cast truth to the ground not because truth is unimportant, but because a truth that fuels accusation and dispute is not the truth He desires. The Torah-scholar knows to set aside divisive truth for peace's sake — and paradoxically, this specific yielding is itself the truest path to bringing genuine truth into the world.

Entry 52 distinguishes partial peace from general peace: not harming one's fellow is partial; giving of one's own to another, yielding beyond obligation — that is the general peace. And the same principle applies inward: not sinning is partial inner peace; fully subordinating all bodily desires to the soul is the complete inner peace.

The chapter culminates (entry 65) in the vision of Mashiach: the Second Temple was destroyed through baseless hatred — and the rebuilt Temple will stand on the foundation of love and totality. Eliyahu's mission is to make peace — and through peace the halachah will be clarified and the redemption will come.
